subject: Affordable Housing Trust Ordinance
overview: The Medford City Council passed the first reading of an ordinance establishing an Affordable Housing Trust and approved adding a Traffic and Transportation Director position to the city classification plan. The Council also voted to table a $1.5 million sidewalk construction loan order and held discussions on Fire Department equipment delays and employee health insurance enrollment.

items.title: Condolences for Paul Howard
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution as amended expressing condolences to the family of Paul Howard, former owner of Jim's Market.

items.title: Dedication to Former City Councilor Robert L. Maloney
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution dedicating the meeting to the memory of former City Councilor Robert L. Maloney.

items.title: Common Victualler License for King Boba Tea
items.summary: The Council approved a common victualler license for King Boba Tea at 464B Salem Street.

items.title: Discussion on Fire Department Equipment and Health Insurance
items.summary: The Council discussed Fire Department fleet maintenance delays and employee health insurance onboarding issues, voting to request an emergency meeting with the administration and a review of HR procedures.

items.title: Affordable Housing Trust Ordinance
items.summary: The Council adopted technical amendments and passed the first reading of an ordinance creating an Affordable Housing Trust for the City of Medford.

items.title: Sidewalk Construction and Equipment Loan Order
items.summary: The Council voted to table a $1.5 million sidewalk loan order until March 14, 2023, while requesting legal guidance regarding the city solicitor position and an update on hiring in-house legal counsel.

items.title: Traffic and Transportation Director Classification
items.summary: The Council approved on first reading an ordinance amendment adding the Traffic and Transportation Director position to the city's classification and compensation plan.

items.title: Traffic and Transportation Director Salary Transfer
items.summary: The Council approved transferring $4,175 from DPW highway salaries to engineering salaries to fund the salary differential for the Traffic and Transportation Director position.

items.title: Tabling of Agenda Papers 23-059, 23-060, and 23-061
items.summary: The Council voted to table three agenda papers until the March 14, 2023 regular meeting.

items.title: Acceptance of Donations
items.summary: The Council approved accepting a $1,000 donation for the Fire Department and surplus office furniture donated by The Furniture Trust.

items.title: Garaging and Registration of Parking Enforcement Vehicles
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution requesting that city parking enforcement vehicles be registered and garaged within Massachusetts and Medford.

items.title: Resolution on Waterfront Clear-Cutting
items.summary: The sponsor withdrew a resolution regarding unauthorized waterfront clear-cutting near Hormel Stadium after city officials confirmed an enforcement order had already been served.

items.title: State Highway Ramp Maintenance
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution requesting MassDOT and DCR to perform roadway repairs on state highway ramps in Medford.

items.title: Expiration of SNAP Emergency Allotments
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution requesting that the administration publicize the upcoming expiration of SNAP emergency allotments across municipal communication channels.

items.title: Resolution Supporting PILOT Reform Legislation
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution endorsing state legislation regarding payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) from tax-exempt organizations.

items.title: Update on Opioid Settlement Proceeds
items.summary: The Council received an update confirming the city's eligibility and planned public engagement regarding national opioid litigation settlement proceeds.

items.title: Planned Development District Fee Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: The Council approved on first reading an ordinance amendment instituting a fee of five cents per square foot over 5,000 square feet for Planned Development District applications.

items.title: Social Justice Roadmap Progress Update
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution requesting an update from the administration on the progress of the city's Social Justice Roadmap.

items.title: Racial Equity Study Request
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution requesting that the city administration conduct an updated racial equity study.

items.title: Referral of Welcoming City Ordinance
items.summary: The Council voted to refer the consideration of a Welcoming City Ordinance to the Subcommittee on Racial Justice, Disabilities, and Elder Affairs.
